"Single-particle steering" represents the most enigmatic form of quantum nonlocality, surpassing both Bell nonlocality and EPR locality violations. This form of "single-particle nonlocality" serves as evidence that single-system quantum states can exhibit "truly nonlocal" behavior, generating statistics in certain multi-party configurations where single-local realism falls short. This paper introduces a novel approach to the containment problem for extended regular expressions, enhancing basic regex capabilities with intersection and complementation while handling infinite alphabets via potentially limitless character sets.
